how.title: How it works
how.intro: This JSON to HTML converter turns a pasted response or local file into semantic HTML. Choose Table for data you want to scan across rows, or List for a document with many levels. Conversion happens in a Web Worker in your browser. The JSON text is not sent to our server, and you do not need an account.
how.arrayObjectsResult: One table with a header row. Columns include every key seen across the objects, in first-seen order. Missing values leave empty cells.
how.objectResult: A two-column table with keys in row headers and their values beside them.
how.nestedResult: A nested table for objects or arrays of objects. An array of simple values becomes a list inside its cell.
how.simple: A simple value or array of simple values
how.simpleResult: A single-cell table, or a one-column table for an array. Null and empty values leave empty cells.
how.layouts: Use Table for records such as orders, contacts and API responses. Use List when the hierarchy matters more than columns: objects become definition lists, and arrays become unordered lists. You can switch layouts after converting without pasting again. In either layout, the result uses text content only. Characters that could form HTML markup are escaped, so a value such as an image tag appears as text.
how.outputs: Table only gives you an HTML fragment to paste into a CMS, email template or existing page. Full HTML page adds a document wrapper, a title, a viewport setting and a small table style. Download that version if you want to open the result as a standalone file. Preview shows the HTML in a sandboxed frame; HTML code shows what will be copied or downloaded.
how.limits: You can paste text or choose a .json or .txt file up to 50 MB. The preview shows at most 500 top-level rows to keep the page responsive; copying and downloading use the complete result. For very large output, the code panel shows only the start, but Copy HTML and Download HTML file still use everything. Numbers keep their JSON spelling. When a browser cannot preserve a large integer through JSON.parse, the converter keeps its original digits and shows a warning.
how.errors: If the JSON cannot be parsed, the message points to a line and column and suggests a fix. Common causes are trailing commas, single quotes, unquoted keys and comments. JSON Lines files contain one value per line rather than a single JSON array; use Wrap lines into an array to convert them, then run the conversion again.

excel.howIntro: Choose a workbook and it is read by a Web Worker in your browser. The file is not uploaded, and you don’t need an account. Pick a sheet, check the preview, then download the CSV. For a workbook with several sheets, Download all sheets as ZIP gives you one CSV per sheet, each named after its sheet.
excel.howNumbersResult: As shown in Excel keeps each cell’s format, such as $1,234.50, 12.5% or a ZIP code with its leading zero. Plain numbers gives 1234.5 and 0.125. Cells with the General format keep up to 15 significant digits either way, as Excel stores them.
excel.howDatesResult: ISO 8601: 2024-01-15, 2024-01-15 14:30:00, or 14:30:00 for a time on its own. Apps read this the same way whatever the date order in your country.
excel.howFormulasResult: The result Excel saved with the file. The formula itself is not included.
excel.howMergedResult: The value goes in the first cell of the merged area. The other cells are empty.
excel.howHiddenResult: Included, as when Excel saves a CSV. Hidden sheets are marked in the sheet list.
excel.howFormattingResult: Left out. A CSV holds only values.
excel.howSeparators: Comma is the standard CSV separator and works in most apps and databases. Pick Semicolon for Excel in countries that use a comma as the decimal mark, such as Germany, France, Spain and Brazil, or when an importer asks for it. Tab gives you a .tsv file, which helps when your values contain many commas. A value that contains the separator, a double quote or a line break is wrapped in double quotes, as RFC 4180 describes, and each row ends with CRLF.
excel.howEncoding: The file is UTF-8, so accented letters, other scripts and emoji come through. Pick UTF-8 with BOM if you will open the CSV in Excel: without the byte order mark, Excel for Windows can show characters such as é as Ã©. Leave it off for databases, code and most import forms, where the BOM can end up in the first column name.
excel.howLimits: You can convert .xlsx, .xlsm, .xlsb, .xls and .ods files up to 50 MB. Large workbooks take longer on a phone and can run out of memory there; a computer handles more. The preview shows the first 100 rows and 30 columns, and the download has everything. Empty rows and columns at the end of a sheet are trimmed, and every row has the same number of fields.
excel.howErrors: A password-protected workbook can’t be read, so remove the password in Excel first. If a file can’t be read, it may be damaged, or it may be another format saved with an Excel extension: open it in Excel and save it as .xlsx. Some apps save formulas without their results, and those cells come out empty; open and save the file in Excel to calculate them.
